snippet.title: How Investors "Short" the Market... (and how you can too)
snippet.description:
Have you seen the film The Big Short? In the film, Michael Burry (played by Christian Bale) makes millions by successfully shorting the housing market just before the 2008 Financial Crisis. 

But when we say he shorted the market, what does this actually mean?

Normally in the world of investing, investors makes money when the stock market goes up. This is called Value Investing. But short sellers make money when the stock market goes down. 

How does this work?

Shorting the market (also known as short selling) is about predicting when the market is overvalued, and betting against it. It's a risky business - and definitely not for beginner investors - but in this video we'll explain how it works, and how you can short the market too. 

Quick disclaimer - this isn't an endorsement of short selling. I am not a financial advisor and this isn't financial advice. You should always do your own research before investing - and you should be very careful with short selling in particular!

snippet.title: The Tribute System: The new World Order
snippet.description:
The world order is definitely changing, but it happens at a pace like watching a child grow—the evolutionary change can almost be elusive to us.

Today, we are seeing a shift in the perception of the United States and its willingness to endure the high costs of war. This shift is leading world leaders to view the US as potentially less reliable in enforcing the global order, which fundamentally impacts international alliances. At the same time, we have a rising power in China. 

We are moving away from a strictly American world order. As we enter this new era, we must find ways to resolve conflicts without the use of the military, and understanding systems like China's traditional approach is in all of our interests. I cover these topics and more in my latest article here: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/tribute-system-new-world-order-ray-dalio-kraac

snippet.title: Central Bank Digital Currencies: Should We Be Afraid?
snippet.description:
Central Bank Digital Currencies, otherwise known as CBDCs, may be where our economic system is heading. Governments want to reshape our financial system around CBDCs, but there are serious concerns that this may lead to authoritarianism and tyranny. People are worried Digital ID, Social Credit Scores and Central Bank Digital Currencies could create and Orwellian surveillance state.

But there is a something opposing Central Bank Digital Currencies. These are called Stablecoins. They can be thought of as a kind of cryptocurrency pegged to real world assets. Stablecoins could be a way for private companies and the free society to push back against this encroaching totalitarianism. 

In this video, we'll explain everything you need to know about Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) and Stablecoins, and where our future may be heading.

The SpaceX IPO will be the biggest in history, and it's set to make Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. But if we look deeper, we find that the SpaceX IPO story is bigger than rockets and Mars, even Elon Musk himself. It shows something quite worrying about the stock market.

snippet.title: Where is Mitch McConnell?
snippet.description:
Where is Mitch McConnell?

The 84-year-old senator has been hospitalized for weeks, but his office has shared very little information about his condition. Meanwhile, rumors are spreading online, lawmakers say they've spoken with him, and people are left wondering what's really going on.

The Senate is trying to move a major housing bill forward, but President Trump says he won't sign it unless lawmakers first pass his SAVE America Act. With a key vote expected early next week, McConnell's absence is adding even more uncertainty to an already high-stakes moment.

snippet.title: US Financial Health & The Debt Cycle
snippet.description:
When debt levels reach extreme sizes relative to income, governments are left with a limited set of choices. They can cut spending, raise taxes, restructure the debt, or print money.

History shows that most systems end up relying heavily on the last option, but printing money doesn’t eliminate the problem–it just shifts how the debt cycle plays out.

Understanding this dynamic is key to understanding the economic environment we’re in.

snippet.title: Private Credit Is Booming... That's The Problem
snippet.description:
Private credit has become one of the fastest-growing corners of finance. 

But underneath the surface, it has some serious issues.

Around 11.5% of private credit loans now include PIK features, which is an increase of more than 72% percent since the end of 2021. 

Meaning instead of paying interest in cash, the unpaid interest gets added to the loan balance, allowing the borrower to postpone payments while the debt continues to grow.

It creates a system where losses can keep growing, while everything still appears healthy on the surface.

#finance #stockmarket #investing #wallstreet

snippet.title: You Can't Stop the Flow of Oil
snippet.description:
Ever wondered how millions of barrels of “illegal” oil keep moving around the world without getting caught? 🛢️⚓️

Welcome to the **Shadow Fleet**.

From the chaotic waters of the Bosporus Strait to shady ship-to-ship transfers out in the middle of the ocean, this is the wild, high-stakes world of the shadow oil market. In this video, we dive into the “Smuggler’s Paradise” that global sanctions have created — where a single $75 million cargo can hinge on one piece of paper.

We’ll explore why 20-year-old rust-bucket tankers are suddenly skipping the scrapyard for a $15 million payday, how landlocked countries like Bolivia end up issuing “Flags of Convenience,” and the infamous “Apartheid Premium” that helped Marc Rich build his billions. Turns out, if you’ve got a ship, a hidden transponder, and a clean Bill of Lading… you can move almost anything if the price is right.

### In this video:

- **The Bosporus Chokepoint**: Why 28 ships and 20 million barrels of oil got jammed up in a half-mile-wide channel  
- **The Shadow Fleet**: Why the number of scrapped tankers suddenly dropped after Russian oil sanctions hit  
- **Flags of Convenience**: How countries with no navy — and sometimes no coastline — help smugglers stay invisible  
- **The Paper Trail**: How ship-to-ship transfers and “ON ORDERS” paperwork make the oil’s origin disappear  
- **The Marc Rich Playbook**: How the “Greatest Oil Smuggler” turned the spot market into a billion-dollar game

snippet.title: The Debt / Credit System
snippet.description: The credit system functions like a circulatory system that delivers nutrients and buying power to various parts of the economy. A system is considered healthy when borrowed money is used to generate productivity, which in turn produces income. However, it becomes unhealthy when debts and debt service costs increase relative to income. This debt service acts like plaque in the circulatory system, squeezing out spending. Because one individual's debt represents another individual's asset, with holders expecting a good return, increased selling leads to supply and demand issues. When combined with high debt service, it ultimately impairs the system's mechanics.
